title: Zahle applies for telephone network and power concession
why: Earliest mention of a telephone network in Lebanon, in an Ottoman-era concession context.

title: Radio Liban begins broadcasting under the Mandate
why: Start of state radio; the broadcast tradition later carried by the Ministry of Information. Founded 1938 as Radio Orient under the Mandate.

title: Radio Orient concession nationalised into Ogero
why: Created the state body that still runs fixed-line and internet wholesale.

title: Israeli invasion disrupts Beirut communications
why: Wartime damage to exchanges set the pattern of repeated network outages in later wars. 1982 siege of West Beirut: phone lines down, communication with outside rare.

title: MTV Lebanon starts broadcasting
why: Post-war private TV boom begins alongside LBC, before the 1994 audiovisual law.

title: Future TV starts broadcasting under Rafik Hariri
why: Third major private channel; illustrates post-war politically-owned media.

title: Cellis and LibanCell win the two GSM contracts
why: Private BOT duopoly shaped prices for a decade; contracts cancelled in 2001.

title: Lebanon has about 200,000 cellular users
why: Uptake data point placing Lebanon ahead in Arab mobile adoption.

title: Al-Manar begins satellite broadcasting
why: Lebanese channel reaches pan-Arab audience during the South withdrawal period.

title: State takes over mobile networks after BOT cancellation
why: Interim state-owned operators MIC1 and MIC2 run the networks pending new contracts. BTO terminated 31 Aug 2002; MIC1 set up 2002 under network custody contract.

title: Orascom and Zain win mobile management contracts
why: Operators managed, not owned, by foreign firms: state ownership continues.

title: Orascom acquires MIC1 management stake
why: Consolidates Alfa's management under Orascom Telecom Media and Technology.

title: Ministry starts fibre backbone installation at $166M
why: First national fibre programme; later phases reached homes only after 2018.

title: Cabinet sets 2 Mbit/s minimum and cuts internet prices
why: First regulated speed floor and price cut after the IMEWE capacity dispute.

title: mtc touch rebranded as Touch
why: Brand change; ownership note: networks stayed state-owned, not nationalised in 2012.

title: Three local firms win $283M fibre distribution contracts
why: Fibre-to-the-home plan that Ogero says reached 221,000 homes in 2024.

title: Parliament committee declines to extend operator contracts
why: Ends the Orascom and Zain management era in 2020. Parliamentary ICT committee decided Dec 2019 not to extend OTMT and Zain contracts.

title: State resumes direct management of Alfa
why: Alfa returns under the ministry in early September 2020; Touch follows on 30 October.

title: State takes Touch back from Zain
why: Completes the return of both networks to direct state control.

title: Port blast damages Beirut offices including tech firms
why: Gemmayzeh and Mar Mikhael startup and media offices hit; ecosystem set back.

title: Lebanon operators warn of shutdown from fuel and funding gaps
why: Crisis-era risk that towers fail without diesel; recurring theme until 2024. Arab News 6 Oct 2021: committee warned telecoms could collapse within days over diesel (corrected from 2022-09)

title: Cyber attack disrupts Ogero services
why: State provider hit by a cyber incident during the Gaza-related border war.

title: Telecom worker killed repairing equipment in south
why: Israeli strikes on the south damaged towers and cut service for villages. Strike at Teir Harfa killed a technician contracted by Touch, 10 May 2024.

title: Strike destroys internet station at Al-Zahrani
why: Villages cut off; by early October 113 Touch and 114 Alfa stations were down. SMEX states an airstrike destroyed the main internet station in Al-Zahrani villages on 'Monday, October 1' (1 Oct 2024 was a Tuesday); 113/114 station counts not confirmed.

title: Pager and radio device explosions across Lebanon
why: Electronic-device attacks made communications gear a security issue for the state.

title: Ookla: fixed broadband ranks 142nd at 12.8 Mbps
why: Median speeds rose about 36% in 2024 but Lebanon stays near the bottom globally.

title: Starlink decree signed: two-year non-exclusive licence
why: Fixed $25,000 yearly fee plus 25% of gross revenue; licence later widened in March 2026. (Decree date: enmaeya gives 8 Oct 2025; L'Orient Today says signed on a Tuesday, i.e. 7 Oct; one-day uncertainty.)

title: Starlink business launch promised for mid-May to mid-June
why: Trade press reported a business-only launch; TRA keeps residential use blocked.

title: TRA FAQ: residential Starlink and global roaming stay blocked
why: Service limited to businesses, NGOs, government and embassies; status conflicts across sources.

title: ArabNet conference circuit includes Beirut edition
why: Regional digital conference series that later anchored Beirut startup networking. First ArabNet conference held in Beirut 25-26 Mar 2010.

title: Bookwitty.com consumer platform launches (company born of Beirut firms Levant Distributors and Keeward)
why: Lebanese-founded social publishing platform; early BDD-era consumer startup. (corrected from 2014: Publishers Weekly says Bookwitty.com launched in 2015; company created 2007 by Beirut firms, later Paris-based)

title: Instabeat swim wearable startup emerges from Lebanon
why: Hardware startup among early Circular 331-era consumer products.

title: Cherpa startup founded in Beirut
why: Lebanese marketplace startup of the BDD-era cohort; fate unverified.

title: Whish Money wallet launches
why: Early Lebanese mobile wallet, positioned before the 2019 banking freeze. Sources give 2017 or 2018 app launch; WOO CASH SAL registered 2019, renamed Whish Money Jan 2021.

title: Nabil Bukhalid inducted into Internet Hall of Fame
why: Lebanese internet pioneer recognised globally.

title: Protests begin; tech firms face bank limits and fuel shortages
why: Start of the 17 October movement and the capital-controls era that hit foreign-paid tech work.

title: BDL authorises e-wallet services
why: Regulatory opening for digital wallets during the crisis. Intermediate Decision 13338 of 21 Jun 2021 (Circular 588) opened e-wallets to everyone; Circular 539 (Jan 2020) covered bank-account holders (corrected from 2021-02)

title: Anghami SPAC merger with Vistas Media announced
why: Path to Nasdaq listing for the first Lebanese-founded tech company there.

title: Toters Series B closes over $15M
why: Largest Lebanon-founded consumer tech round of the crisis period.

title: MENA VC funding falls; Lebanon raises about $1M in 12 deals
why: Lebanon's funding share collapsed after the banking crisis.

title: StartupBlink ranks Lebanon 77th globally with 78 startups
why: Small but resilient ecosystem; tracker totals differ from MAGNiTT.

title: Cabinet approves draft law for a Ministry of Technology and AI
why: First Arab-league-style AI ministry proposal in Lebanon awaits parliament.

title: National AI Framework goes to consultation
why: Step toward a drafted national AI strategy. (corrected from 2026-01: MITAI deck updated 5 Mar 2026 lists the National AI Framework as under consultation; start of consultation not stated)

title: Experia innovation expo scheduled at Forum de Beyrouth
why: MITAI-backed showcase planned 8-10 October 2026. Site: 8-10 Oct 2026, Forum de Beyrouth, organiser Promofair, supported by MITAI.

title: USJ publishes Master in Artificial Intelligence catalogue
why: One of the first taught AI master's programmes in a Lebanese university.

title: LAU offers online MS in Applied Artificial Intelligence
why: 30-credit, two-year online AI degree.

title: Phoenicia University and AUT sign MITAI memoranda
why: Universities join the ministry's AI training drive.

title: Greater Lebanon proclaimed; telegraph and post under Mandate
why: Mandate-era ministries of post and telegraph set the base for later Ogero. Page: Inspection Generale des Postes et Telegraphes formed 1 Jan 1921 for Lebanon and Syria; Greater Lebanon proclamation itself not on page.

title: Hassan Kamel Al-Sabbah dies; Nabatieh-born GE inventor
why: Lebanese-born engineer with 100+ US patents, an early diaspora tech figure.

title: Michael Atiyah wins Fields Medal
why: British mathematician of Lebanese descent, a diaspora science milestone.

title: Elias James Corey wins Nobel Prize in Chemistry
why: Lebanese-American chemist of Lebanese parentage.

title: Dial-up internet becomes commercial
why: Early commercial ISP days; see existing entry for licences.

title: State cancels Cellis and LibanCell contracts
why: Ends the BOT duopoly after disputes over revenue share. Contracts terminated June 2001; effective 31 Aug 2002.

title: IMEWE cable lands; capacity dispute follows
why: Submarine cable opens bandwidth; ministry-Ogero dispute delays consumer benefit.

title: Rafik Hariri assassination transforms Future TV
why: Future TV moves from owner channel to political symbol; later sold down.

title: OTV launches
why: New partisan TV entrant to the crowded Lebanese market. Began broadcasting 20 Jul 2007 on Arabsat; official launch 2008.

title: KAUST opens in Saudi Arabia
why: Gulf investment in a research university; context for Lebanese brain drain to the Gulf.

title: Beirut Digital District launches
why: Dedicated tech zone in Beirut's Mar Mikhael and Bourj Hammoud area.

title: Gulf states invest heavily after GPT-4 release
why: Gulf sovereign funds begin AI infrastructure pivot.

title: TII releases Falcon 180B
why: UAE open-weight model briefly tops open LLM leaderboards. Announced 6 Sep 2023.

title: Microsoft invests $1.5bn in G42
why: US-UAE alignment on AI hardware and standards.

title: MGX fund created in Abu Dhabi for AI investing
why: Mubadala and G42 back a vehicle targeting global AI infrastructure.

title: US-Saudi AI agreements signed during Trump visit
why: HUMAIN deals with Nvidia, AMD and others.

title: MBZUAI and G42 release K2 Think
why: 32B open reasoning system from the UAE. Announced 9 Sep 2025, 32B parameters.

title: US approves up to 35,000 GB300 systems each for HUMAIN and G42
why: Export-control relief after the Saudi Crown Prince's Washington visit. Approved 19 Nov 2025, up to 35,000 GB300-equivalents each.

title: Qatar launches Qai and $20bn Brookfield AI infrastructure venture
why: Qatar enters the Gulf AI race via QIA.

title: Stargate UAE first phase guided for Q3 2026
why: 200 MW first phase of the 1 GW G42 OpenAI Oracle Nvidia cluster.

title: MBZUAI releases K2 Think V2, 70B open reasoning model
why: Presented as fully open across data, training and evaluation.

title: HUMAIN begins private AI data-centre build with MIS contract
why: SR 1.88bn (about $501M) 12-month build starting February 2026. Contract about SR1.88bn ($501m), 12 months, signing expected 15 Feb 2026.

title: GPT-5.5 reported released
why: Aggregator-reported date; verify against OpenAI before quoting.
drop_reason: unconfirmed model release: aggregator blog only, no vendor page

title: Claude Fable 5.1 reported released
why: Aggregator-reported date; verify against Anthropic before quoting.

title: GPT-6 Astra reported released
why: Aggregator-reported date; verify against OpenAI before quoting.
drop_reason: unconfirmed model release: aggregator blog only, no vendor page

title: Shehadi reports 2,500 residents in Zaka AI training
why: MITAI outreach figure reported by The National.

title: OSN tables $3.39 per share take-private bid for Anghami
why: OSN owns about 67%; special committee of independent directors formed.

title: UAE names Omar Al Olama Minister of State for AI
why: First AI minister globally; model for Lebanon's 2025 MITAI.

title: Saudi Vision 2030 unveiled with tech diversification goals
why: Policy frame behind later SDAIA and HUMAIN.

title: Anghami lists on Nasdaq
why: Existing entry confirmed; adds SEC filing as better source. Trading began 4 Feb 2022; business combination closed 3 Feb.
dup_of: Anghami starts trading on Nasdaq via SPAC

title: Claude 3 family released by Anthropic
why: Frontier model milestone used as a global AI marker.

title: DeepSeek-R1 paper and release
why: Low-cost open reasoning model reshapes the compute-cost debate for sovereign AI.
